title: The Smoothing
lines: The Smoothing examines how truthful language can still hide decision-relevant consequences.
Its central question is what disappears when a message becomes easier to accept.
The book compares source and output through actors, uncertainty, alternatives, and affected people.
It treats smoothing as a research hypothesis, including useful simplification and harmful attenuation.
Readers learn to question apparent completeness without demanding that every text preserve every detail.

title: True, but missing the consequence
lines: A description may preserve an event while losing who bears its cost.
A conflict can become a generic challenge without stating a false fact.
The book asks which lost distinctions would change a reader's decision.
Useful compression remains possible when important consequences stay recoverable.
That distinction prevents its proposed category from condemning every act of simplification.

title: A hypothesis needs a comparison
lines: The proposed research compares transformations against sources, tasks, audiences, and relevant consequences.
It must distinguish smoothing from neighboring concepts such as bias, omission, and sycophancy.
The book proposes complementary instruments rather than one universal detector.
Its preliminary aggregate risk formula is explicitly unvalidated.
Readers are asked to examine whether the category yields useful, falsifiable distinctions.

title: Read what the polish removes
lines: Begin with the prologue and the distinction between useful and harmful simplification.
Then inspect the measurement proposals before accepting the book's broader applications.
The literary demonstrations explore possible experiences rather than establishing empirical findings.
The Smoothing is useful for keeping actors, alternatives, and consequences inside an apparently complete account.
Read it to ask what a smoother formulation made harder to notice or recover.
